key_insight: Mode connectivity in quantum machine learning is best understood on the reachable unitary Lie group, where low-loss regions can be path-connected independently of the specific parameterization.
engineering_relevance: This gives quantum circuit designers a geometric way to diagnose and exploit trainable low-loss regions, especially in overparameterized ansätze where unitary-space connectivity can be lifted back to parameter space.
method: Formulate mode connectivity on the reachable unitary Lie group generated by the dynamical Lie algebra.
Assume a near-minimum connected low-loss band with no critical values to prove path-connectedness of the sublevel set.
Use overparameterization to lift Lie-group paths to parameter-space trajectories for practical observability.
evidence_signal: Toy numerical experiments show geodesic interpolations between trained unitaries with nearly zero loss barriers, matching the proposed Lie-group interpretation.
watch_item: The result relies on a near-minimum connectedness assumption and absence of critical values in the low-loss band, so it may not hold for all ansätze or loss landscapes.
paper_title: Lie-Group Mode Connectivity in Quantum Machine Learning from a Dynamical Lie Algebra Perspective
